# Personal data map

Where Plux stores personal data, how long it is kept and what a data subject request does to it (`SEC-162`). An administrator with `dsr.manage` exports or erases a device or a pseudonymous user with `plux dsr export` and `plux dsr erase`.

Audit entries are never erased, because deleting one breaks the hash chain (`SEC-140`). They carry only pseudonymous identifiers, and a data subject request is recorded as an entry that names the subject by hash.

## Erased by a data subject request

| Store | Holds | Device key | User key | Personal fields | Retention | Erase | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `telemetry_events` | Runtime telemetry events of the first analytics tables, kept for existing installations. | `device_id` | — | `device_id`, `fields` | Raw-event retention, 13 months by default and configurable per organisation (ANL-011). | delete | Declared, non-sensitive event properties only; the events are the device's. |
| `analytics_events` | Raw analytics events, partitioned by month. | `device_id` | — | `device_id`, `locale`, `device_class`, `fields` | Raw-event retention, 13 months by default and configurable per organisation (ANL-011). | delete | Erased row-wise across every partition. |
| `device_push_tokens` | The push token of a device, sealed with envelope encryption (SEC-106). | `device_id` | — | `ciphertext`, `wrapped_key` | Until the device is erased or its app or organisation is deleted. | delete | Export reports that a token is held and its provider; the token itself is never returned. |
| `device_sca_keys` | The public key a device enrolled for strong customer authentication (SEC-027). | `device_id` | — | `device_id`, `public_key`, `jkt` | Until the device is erased or its app or organisation is deleted. | delete | — |
| `device_tokens` | Short-lived device access tokens, stored as hashes. | `device_id` | — | `device_id`, `secret_hash` | Until the token expires, then the maintenance sweep. | delete | Deleting them revokes the device's sessions. |
| `error_group_devices` | Which devices an error group was seen on, for its affected-device count (ANL-040). | `device_id` | — | `device_id` | Until the device is erased or its app or organisation is deleted. | delete | — |
| `device_bundles` | The bundles a device reported holding. | `device_id` | — | `device_id` | Until the device is erased or its app or organisation is deleted. | delete | — |
| `devices` | The device record: platform, versions, locale, hardware-bound key, attestation result and revocation. | `id` | — | `id`, `os_version`, `locale`, `device_class`, `dpop_public_key`, `app_attest_public_key`, `agreement_public_key` | Until the device is erased or its app or organisation is deleted. | delete | Erased last. With the record and its credentials gone, the device has to register again. |
| `notifications` | The in-app inbox of a user. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `title`, `body` | Until the notification is dropped or the user is deleted. | delete | — |
| `notification_subscriptions` | What a user or team subscribed to. | — | `subject_id` | `subject_id` | Until the subscription is removed or the organisation is deleted. | delete | Only subscriptions whose subject_kind is user; team subscriptions name no person. |

## Aggregates and retained records

| Store | Holds | Device key | User key | Personal fields | Retention | Erase | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `analytics_rollups` | Five-minute and coarser aggregates of the events by dimension. | — | — | `locale` | Indefinite, configurable per organisation (ANL-011). | aggregate | Aggregate only: counts and histograms with no device or user identifier. A subject contributes through its raw events, which are erased; buckets already summed are not recomputed. |
| `function_invocations` | One row per run of a server function. | — | — | — | Function-log retention, the telemetry retention of the organisation (FN-032). | aggregate | Holds no input, output, user or device; there is no identifier to erase by. |
| `function_logs` | Lines a server function logged. | — | — | — | Function-log retention, the telemetry retention of the organisation (FN-032). | retained | No column names a subject. The lines are what the function wrote, so functions must not log personal data; the rows expire with the retention. |
| `audit_log` | The hash-chained audit log. | — | — | `actor_id`, `source_ip`, `user_agent` | Audit retention, 10 years by default for production data (SEC-143); never erased (SEC-140). | retained | Never erased, because deleting an entry breaks the chain (SEC-140). Entries carry only pseudonymous identifiers: actors are identified by their identifier and a display name that is never an email address, devices and data subjects by identifier or hash. A data subject request is recorded here as an entry that names the subject by hash. |
| `dsr_requests` | The completed data subject requests. | — | — | `subject_hash` | Audit retention, 10 years by default for production data (SEC-143); never erased (SEC-140). | retained | Holds the subject's hash only, never the identifier. |
| `dsr_tombstones` | What an erasure left behind: subject hash, store, row count and time. | — | — | `subject_hash` | Audit retention, 10 years by default for production data (SEC-143); never erased (SEC-140). | retained | The proof that an erasure happened; it holds the subject's hash only. |
| `idempotency_keys` | Stored responses of retried requests, sealed. | — | — | `subject` | The idempotency window, then the maintenance sweep. | retained | Short-lived and sealed (SEC-106); the subject is the credential that made the request. |

## Staff account data

| Store | Holds | Device key | User key | Personal fields | Retention | Erase | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `users` | Staff accounts. | — | — | `email`, `display name`, `password_hash` | While the account exists. | account | Removed when an administrator deletes the user. The account is not a pseudonymous data subject: it is identified by email. |
| `memberships` | Which organisations and teams a user belongs to. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `role_grants` | Roles bound to a user at a scope. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `app_access` | Per-app access of a user. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `sessions` | Signed-in sessions of a user. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `secret_hash`, `ip_prefix`, `user_agent` | Until the session expires or is revoked. | account | — |
| `mfa_factors` | Second factors a user enrolled. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `mfa_challenges` | Pending second-factor challenges. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | Minutes; the maintenance sweep removes expired ones. | account | — |
| `access_tokens` | API tokens; a CI token names the workload it was minted for. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `subject`, `last_ip_prefix`, `last_user_agent` | Until the token expires or is revoked. | account | — |
| `step_up_requests` | WebAuthn step-up ceremonies of a user and the CLI grants they issued (SEC-103); only hashes of their secrets. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `jkt` | Minutes; a request or grant expires five minutes after it is made. | account | — |
| `user_identities` | The single-sign-on identities linked to a user. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `subject` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `federated_sign_ins` | The single-sign-on sign-ins of a user, by issuer and subject. | — | `user_id` | `user_id`, `subject` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `federated_assignments` | The grants and team memberships an identity provider's mapping gave a user. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |
| `scim_users` | The users a SCIM client provisioned. | — | `user_id` | `user_id` | While the account exists. | account | — |

## Named like personal data, but not personal

| Store | Holds | Device key | User key | Personal fields | Retention | Erase | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translation_locks` | The editing lock of one locale of an app's translations. | — | — | — | Until released or taken over. | none | locale is the language being translated, not a person's locale. |
| `golden_cases` | Golden-test cases of an app. | — | — | — | Until the case is deleted. | none | locale is the language the case renders in, not a person's locale. |
